title: Hebrews Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 12.

questions.question: In Hebrews 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Let us lay aside every weight
Ye have not yet resisted unto blood
For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth
questions.correctAnswer: Let us lay aside every weight
questions.explanation: This command appears first in the chapter as it is the opening action for the believers.

questions.question: Who is described as the author and finisher of our faith?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus
questions.explanation: This description of Jesus appears in Hebrews 12:2.

questions.question: What should we do with the sin that easily besets us?
questions.correctAnswer: Lay it aside
questions.explanation: We are instructed to lay aside the sin that easily besets us in Hebrews 12:1.

questions.question: What did Jesus endure for the joy set before him?
questions.correctAnswer: The cross
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:2 states that Jesus endured the cross for the joy set before him.

questions.question: What should we consider to avoid becoming wearied and faint in our minds?
options: Him that endured such contradiction of sinners
questions.correctAnswer: Him that endured such contradiction of sinners
questions.explanation: We are encouraged to consider Him in Hebrews 12:3 to avoid weariness.

questions.question: To what extent have we resisted against sin?
questions.correctAnswer: Unto blood
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:4 mentions that we have not yet resisted unto blood in striving against sin.

questions.question: What does the Lord do for whom He loves?
questions.correctAnswer: He chastens them
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:6 states that whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.

questions.question: What is the purpose of chastening according to the Lord?
questions.correctAnswer: For our profit
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:10 explains that chastening is for our profit.

questions.question: What kind of correction did our earthly fathers give us?
questions.correctAnswer: After their own pleasure
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in Hebrews 12:10 regarding the correction from our earthly fathers.

questions.question: What are we encouraged not to despise?
questions.correctAnswer: The chastening of the Lord
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:5 advises us not to despise the chastening of the Lord.

questions.question: If we endure chastening, how does God deal with us?
questions.correctAnswer: As sons
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:7 states that if we endure chastening, God deals with us as with sons.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord chastens those He loves.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:6 confirms that the Lord chastens whom He loves.

questions.question: True or False: We have not resisted against sin at all.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:4 mentions that we have not yet resisted unto blood, implying we have resisted to some degree.

questions.question: True or False: God chastens only those who are not His children.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text states that God chastens those He loves, indicating they are His children, as seen in Hebrews 12:6.

questions.question: True or False: We are encouraged to ignore the corrections from the Lord.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:5 advises against despising the chastening of the Lord, indicating we should pay attention to it.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 12:11, what does chastening yield afterward to those who are exercised by it?
questions.correctAnswer: The peaceable fruit of righteousness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:11 explains that chastening, though grievous at present, afterward yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness to those exercised by it.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 12:13 promise will happen if someone 'lifts up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees' as commanded in Hebrews 12:12?
options: Makes straight paths for their feet and heals the lame
questions.correctAnswer: Makes straight paths for their feet and heals the lame
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:13 states that making straight paths for your feet, which follows the exhortation in verse 12, leads to healing the lame rather than turning them out of the way.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Hebrews 12:15 for those who fail to look diligently lest any root of bitterness spring up?
options: They will be cast out of the church
questions.correctAnswer: Many are defiled
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:15 warns that failure to watch diligently can cause a root of bitterness to spring up, troubling others and leading to many being defiled.

questions.question: How do Hebrews 12:16 and 12:17 connect the example of Esau with the theme of repentance and consequences?
options: Esau sold his birthright for a morsel of meat and later found no place of repentance when seeking the blessing
Esau was forgiven despite selling his birthright
Esau repented and regained his birthright
Esau was a model of patience and endurance
questions.correctAnswer: Esau sold his birthright for a morsel of meat and later found no place of repentance when seeking the blessing
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:16 describes Esau selling his birthright for a morsel of meat, and verse 17 explains he was rejected when seeking the blessing later because he found no place of repentance despite seeking it carefully with tears.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 12:14, what two things must we pursue to see the Lord?
options: Peace with all men and holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Peace with all men and holiness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:14 commands believers to follow peace with all men and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.

questions.question: What practical action does Hebrews 12:12 recommend for those who are weak or discouraged?
options: Lift up the hands which hang down and strengthen feeble knees
questions.correctAnswer: Lift up the hands which hang down and strengthen feeble knees
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:12 instructs believers to lift up hands that hang down and strengthen feeble knees, encouraging perseverance and renewal of strength.

questions.question: Why should believers 'make straight paths' for their feet, according to Hebrews 12:13?
options: Lest the lame be turned out of the way, but rather be healed
So they may run faster in the race of faith
To follow the example of the saints
questions.correctAnswer: Lest the lame be turned out of the way, but rather be healed
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:13 explains making straight paths for the feet to prevent the lame from being turned out of the way and instead allow them to be healed.

questions.question: What warning does Hebrews 12:15 give about failing to look diligently for anyone who might fail of the grace of God?
options: A root of bitterness may spring up and trouble you, defiling many
You will be judged harshly by God
You will lose your own grace
You will be separated from the church
questions.correctAnswer: A root of bitterness may spring up and trouble you, defiling many
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:15 warns that failing to watch carefully can allow bitterness to take root, causing trouble and defiling many.

questions.question: How is Esau described in Hebrews 12:16, and what does his example teach about integrity?
options: As a fornicator and profane person who sold his birthright for one morsel of meat
As a faithful man who repented quickly
As a strong warrior who protected his family
As an example of patience and endurance
questions.correctAnswer: As a fornicator and profane person who sold his birthright for one morsel of meat
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:16 describes Esau as a fornicator and profane person who traded his birthright for food, illustrating the danger of sacrificing integrity for immediate gain.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 12:17 reveal about Esau's attempt to regain his blessing?
options: He was rejected because he found no place of repentance, despite seeking it with tears
He was immediately forgiven and restored
He received the blessing after much prayer
He never tried to regain it
questions.correctAnswer: He was rejected because he found no place of repentance, despite seeking it with tears
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:17 tells that Esau, when he later sought the blessing, was rejected because he found no place for repentance, even though he sought it carefully with tears.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 12:18, to what kind of mount have believers NOT come?
options: A mount that might be touched, burned with fire, blackness, darkness, and tempest
A mount of peace and rest
A mount of grace and mercy
A mount of blessing and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: A mount that might be touched, burned with fire, blackness, darkness, and tempest
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:18 states that believers have not come to a physical mount characterized by fire, darkness, and tempest, describing the Sinai experience.

questions.question: What sound and voice are described in Hebrews 12:19 as part of the experience at the mount?
options: The sound of a trumpet and the voice of words, which the people begged not to hear anymore
The sound of singing and joyful voices
The voice of angels proclaiming peace
The roar of thunder and lightning
questions.correctAnswer: The sound of a trumpet and the voice of words, which the people begged not to hear anymore
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:19 describes the sound of a trumpet and the voice of words at the mount, which caused those who heard to entreat that the word not be spoken to them again.

questions.question: What was the command regarding touching the mount, as stated in Hebrews 12:20?
options: If a beast touched the mountain, it was to be stoned or pierced with a dart
Everyone was allowed to climb the mountain
Only priests could approach the mountain
The mountain was to be circled seven times
questions.correctAnswer: If a beast touched the mountain, it was to be stoned or pierced with a dart
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:20 explains the strict command that if even a beast touched the mountain, it was to be stoned or thrust through with a dart, showing the holiness and severity of the place.

questions.question: Hebrews 12:2 encourages believers to fix their eyes on whom as the author and finisher of our faith?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:2 states that we must look unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith.

questions.question: Hebrews 12:6 says that the Lord chastens those whom He loves but does not scourge every son He receives.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:6 says the Lord chastens and scourgeth every son whom He receives, indicating all true sons undergo discipline.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 12.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 12:22, to what have the readers come?
options: Mount Sion and the city of the living God
Mount Sinai and the earthly Jerusalem
Mount Zion and the city of the dead
Mount Horeb and the tabernacle of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Sion and the city of the living God
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:22 states, 'But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem...'

questions.question: Who is described as 'the mediator of the new covenant' in Hebrews 12:24?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:24 clearly says, 'And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant...'

questions.question: What does the 'blood of sprinkling' in Hebrews 12:24 speak of according to the verse?
options: Better things than that of Abel
questions.correctAnswer: Better things than that of Abel
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:24 states, '...and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.'

questions.question: What warning is given in Hebrews 12:25 about refusing him that speaketh?
options: If they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape
Those who refuse him shall be forgiven
Refusal will lead to riches and honor
questions.correctAnswer: If they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:25 warns, 'For if they escaped not who refused him that spake on earth, much more shall not we escape...'

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Yet once more' signify in Hebrews 12:27?
options: The removing of those things that are shaken
The establishment of the earthly kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The removing of those things that are shaken
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:27 explains, 'Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken...'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 12:29, how is God described?
questions.correctAnswer: A consuming fire
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:29 states, 'For our God is a consuming fire.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'mediator' (μεσίτης) in Hebrews 12:24 mean?
options: One who reconciles or intervenes between two parties
A prophet who predicts future events
questions.correctAnswer: One who reconciles or intervenes between two parties
questions.explanation: The Greek term μεσίτης (mesitēs) used in Hebrews 12:24 means 'one who mediates or reconciles between two parties,' referring to Jesus as the mediator of the new covenant.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Hebrews 12:22-24 when describing the heavenly city and assembly?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:22-24 uses inclusio by framing the passage with references to the heavenly Jerusalem and the assembly of the firstborn, creating a literary envelope emphasizing the heavenly gathering.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event is echoed by the description of the voice shaking the earth in Hebrews 12:26?
options: The giving of the Law at Mount Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: The giving of the Law at Mount Sinai
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:26 refers to 'Whose voice then shook the earth,' echoing the terrifying theophany at Mount Sinai when God gave the Law (Exodus 19:18-19).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of endurance and looking unto Jesus as found in Hebrews 12:1-2?
questions.correctAnswer: James 1:12
questions.explanation: James 1:12 speaks of the blessing for the one who endures trials, connecting to Hebrews 12:1-2’s emphasis on endurance looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of faith.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Hebrews 12:21, where Moses says, 'I exceedingly fear and quake'?
options: The law’s command that if a beast touches the mountain, it shall be stoned
The exhortation to follow peace and holiness
The description of the heavenly Jerusalem
The warning not to refuse him who speaks
questions.correctAnswer: The law’s command that if a beast touches the mountain, it shall be stoned
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:20 precedes 12:21 and states, 'And if so much as a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned, or thrust through with a dart,' setting the terrifying scene Moses reacts to in 12:21.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 12:11, what does chastening yield to those exercised by it?
questions.correctAnswer: The peaceable fruit of righteousness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:11 explains that chastening 'yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.'

questions.question: In Hebrews 12:16-17, Esau is used as an example of what kind of person?
options: A profane person who sold his birthright for a morsel of meat
A faithful servant who was rewarded
A king who led Israel into battle
questions.correctAnswer: A profane person who sold his birthright for a morsel of meat
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:16-17 describes Esau as 'a profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.'

questions.question: How does Hebrews 12:9 contrast earthly fathers with God the Father?
options: Earthly fathers chastened for a few days, but God chastens for our profit
Earthly fathers are perfect, but God is fallible
Earthly fathers never discipline, but God always punishes
Earthly fathers and God have the same role without difference
questions.correctAnswer: Earthly fathers chastened for a few days, but God chastens for our profit
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:9-10 contrasts that earthly fathers chastened us briefly, but God does so for our profit that we might share in His holiness.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 12:28 instructs believers to receive a kingdom which cannot be moved and to serve God with reverence and godly fear.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:28 says, 'Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear.'

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 12:6 teach about God's nature in relation to His children?
options: God disciplines those He loves as a sign of sonship
God's love is unconditional and without correction
God rejects those who sin repeatedly
questions.correctAnswer: God disciplines those He loves as a sign of sonship
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:6 states, 'For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth,' teaching that God's discipline is an expression of His love toward His children.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning sanctification is taught in Hebrews 12:11?
options: Chastening, though painful, produces the peaceable fruit of righteousness
Sanctification is achieved without suffering or discipline
Chastening is always joyful and easy to bear
Righteousness is imputed without any exercise
questions.correctAnswer: Chastening, though painful, produces the peaceable fruit of righteousness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:11 explains that 'no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby,' highlighting sanctification through discipline.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 12:24 teach about Christ's mediatorial work?
options: Jesus is the mediator of the new covenant and His blood speaks better than Abel’s
Jesus mediates the old covenant through the Law
Christ’s blood is ineffective compared to Abel's
The new covenant is based solely on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the mediator of the new covenant and His blood speaks better than Abel’s
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:24 states, 'And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel,' affirming Christ’s superior mediatorial role.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 12:29 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Consuming fire
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:29 says, 'For our God is a consuming fire,' specifically demonstrating God's attribute as a consuming fire, i.e., His holiness and judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Hebrews 12:26 where God promises to shake not only the earth but also heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:26 reveals God’s sovereign power in shaking both earth and heaven, showing His control over all creation.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 12:22–24 connect to the broader biblical theme of the heavenly Jerusalem?
options: It portrays believers as citizens of the heavenly Jerusalem, fulfilling Old Testament promises of God's eternal city
It minimizes the importance of the heavenly Jerusalem in salvation
It teaches that the earthly Jerusalem is the ultimate hope
It disconnects the church from heavenly realities
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays believers as citizens of the heavenly Jerusalem, fulfilling Old Testament promises of God's eternal city
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:22–24 describes coming to mount Sion, the heavenly Jerusalem, connecting to Old Testament prophetic promises and the eschatological hope for God's people.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Hebrews 12:16–17 make by referencing Esau?
options: It warns against profaning the birthright and losing access to covenant blessings
It praises Esau as a model of repentance
It teaches that birthrights are irrelevant to salvation
It encourages selling spiritual blessings for temporal gain
questions.correctAnswer: It warns against profaning the birthright and losing access to covenant blessings
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:16–17 uses Esau’s example to warn believers against despising spiritual blessings, as Esau lost his birthright and blessing irreversibly.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 12:5 and Hebrews 12:7 teach about God's discipline and sonship?
options: God disciplines His children because He loves them, confirming their status as His sons
Discipline is a sign of God's rejection
God disciplines all people equally regardless of relationship
Discipline is optional and unrelated to sonship
questions.correctAnswer: God disciplines His children because He loves them, confirming their status as His sons
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:5 exhorts not to despise the Lord’s chastening, and 12:7 explains that enduring discipline shows God deals with us as sons, confirming sonship through discipline.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification and perseverance is taught by combining Hebrews 12:1 and Hebrews 12:2?
options: Believers must lay aside sin and run the race with endurance, looking to Jesus as the perfect example and source of faith
Sanctification is passive and requires no effort
Faith is completed solely by human works
Jesus is only a distant example, not actively involved
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must lay aside sin and run the race with endurance, looking to Jesus as the perfect example and source of faith
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:1 calls believers to lay aside sin and run with patience, while 12:2 shows Jesus is the author and finisher of faith, motivating perseverance.

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis about repentance and irrevocable judgment is taught by Hebrews 12:17 and Hebrews 12:25?
options: Those who reject God’s promise cannot find repentance, and turning away from God who speaks from heaven brings severe judgment
Repentance is always possible regardless of rejection
Judgment is delayed indefinitely for all
Rejecting God has no serious consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Those who reject God’s promise cannot find repentance, and turning away from God who speaks from heaven brings severe judgment
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:17 shows Esau found no place for repentance after rejecting his birthright; 12:25 warns refusing Him who speaks from heaven results in judgment.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God's discipline in Hebrews 12:10–11 is punitive and not loving. What does Hebrews 12:10–11 actually teach?
options: God’s discipline is for our profit, producing holiness and the peaceful fruit of righteousness
Discipline is a sign of divine anger without love
God’s discipline is harmful and destructive
questions.correctAnswer: God’s discipline is for our profit, producing holiness and the peaceful fruit of righteousness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:10 teaches God disciplines 'for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness,' and 12:11 confirms it yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness, showing loving purpose.

questions.question: What doctrine about human weakness and divine strengthening is taught in Hebrews 12:12–13?
options: Believers are exhorted to strengthen their weak hands and knees so they do not stray but be healed
Weakness should be ignored and left to worsen
God does not aid those who are weak
Straying from the path has no consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are exhorted to strengthen their weak hands and knees so they do not stray but be healed
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:12–13 encourages lifting up feeble limbs and making straight paths so the lame may be healed, implying God’s help in human weakness.

questions.question: What theological truth about holiness and seeing the Lord is taught in Hebrews 12:14?
options: Holiness is essential; without it no one will see the Lord
Peace and holiness are unrelated to salvation
One can see the Lord without holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness is essential; without it no one will see the Lord
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:14 states, 'Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord,' teaching the necessity of holiness for seeing God.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of the kingdom believers receive is taught in Hebrews 12:28?
options: Believers receive an unshakable kingdom and should serve God with reverence and godly fear
Believers receive a temporary kingdom that can be lost
The kingdom is based on human merit
The kingdom requires no reverence or fear
questions.correctAnswer: Believers receive an unshakable kingdom and should serve God with reverence and godly fear
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:28 teaches that receiving an unshakable kingdom calls for serving God acceptably with reverence and godly fear.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and temptation is taught in Hebrews 12:15?
options: Believers must watch diligently to avoid failing grace and the spread of root bitterness
Sin is inevitable and cannot be guarded against
Bitterness has no effect on the community
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must watch diligently to avoid failing grace and the spread of root bitterness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 12:15 warns to look diligently lest any fail of the grace of God and lest root of bitterness cause defilement, teaching vigilance against sin.
